title: Passing on a concern
intent: Learners can pass on a family member's concern in the order their service expects.
goal: pass on a family member's concern in the right order.
prompt: A family member tells you something that worries you. Put these steps in the order you would take them.

items.label: Listen without interrupting
items.why: You cannot pass on accurately what you did not hear in full.

items.label: Acknowledge what they have said
items.why: It tells them they were heard before anything else happens.

items.label: Tell them you will pass it on, and to whom
items.why: They should never be surprised that someone else knows.

items.label: Tell your supervisor the same shift, in person
items.why: A note alone can sit unread. In person, the same shift, it gets acted on.

items.label: Record it in the progress notes
items.why: The record comes after the conversation with your supervisor, as your service requires.

items.label: Check back with the family that someone has followed up
items.why: Closing the loop is what the family remembers, and it catches the follow-ups that did not happen.

sources.label: Course page: Knowing your role and when to refer
sources.note: The order of steps is from the page. The reasons were written for this activity.
